A state cannot impose registration requirements for cosmetic facilities that differ from or are in addition to federal requirements applicable under the FD&C Act, as such actions would violate the preemption provisions established in section 614(a). Specifically, no State or political subdivision may establish or continue any law, regulation, order, or other requirement for cosmetics that is different from or in addition to, or otherwise not identical with, any federal requirement regarding registration and product listing. This includes requirements related to registration of cosmetic facilities [1].

The FD&C Act § 614(a) [21 U.S.C. 364j(a)] prohibits states from imposing registration requirements different from federal ones [1].  

The available regulatory sources do not provide enough information to answer whether a state may impose other types of non-registration requirements (e.g., inspection, licensing, or fees), as the question specifically concerns registration and only the provision on registration is directly relevant. The text does not address non-registration requirements beyond what is stated in § 614(a).
